firm.

accounts.
(IV) Dissolution of partnership.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Detailed Solution:
1. (A) Termination of business: Leads to complete winding up of the firm -> (III) Dissolution of firm.
2. (B) Continuation of business: Business continues under reconstituted agreement -> (IV) Dissolution of partnership.
3. (C) Intervention of court: Court can order dissolution of a firm under Section 44, but court never orders mere reconstitution/dissolution of partnership -> (I) Not possible in the dissolution of partnership.
4. (D) Continuation of books of accounts: In dissolution of a firm, books are permanently closed; thus continuation of books is -> (II) Not possible in the dissolution of a firm.
5. Matching set: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (C) is the correct match.
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.

questionText:
In which of the following ways does dissolution of a firm take place?
(A) Dissolution by agreement
(B) Compulsory dissolution
(C) On the happening of certain contingencies
(D) Dissolution by notice
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Validates both statements as accurate NCERT facts.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid NCERT facts erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Detailed Solution:
1. (A) Dissolution by agreement (Section 40): With consent of all partners or in accordance with contract.
2. (B) Compulsory dissolution (Section 41): Insolvent partners or business becoming unlawful.
3. (C) On happening of contingencies (Section 42): Expiry of term, death of partner, etc.
4. (D) Dissolution by notice (Section 43): In partnership at will, any partner can give notice in writing.
5. All four options (A, B, C, D) are statutory modes of dissolution.
Hence, option (B) is correct.
Hence, option (A) is correct.

4. (D) Dissolution by notice (Section 43): In partnership at will, any partner can give notice in writing.

Hence, option (A) is correct.
